subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should installed third-party plugins receive durable SQLite keyed storage, and if so should the existing keyed-store API gain an explicit agent-scoped mode rather than introducing a separate `context.cache` contract?
rationale: The current restriction to bundled and trusted official plugins is an intentional capability boundary, while choosing shared plugin KV versus per-agent storage determines data isolation, quotas, lifecycle cleanup, and the permanent public SDK contract.

options.title: Extend Existing Store Safely
options.body: Add an explicit agent-scoped mode to `api.runtime.state.openKeyedStore` with declared capabilities, quotas, isolation, and lifecycle tests before allowing installed plugins to use it.

options.title: Keep Trusted-Only Storage
options.body: Retain the current trusted-plugin restriction and require ordinary external plugins to own their persistence outside the privileged runtime storage facade.

options.title: Add Separate Cache API
options.body: Introduce `context.cache` as a distinct agent-context surface, accepting the maintenance and conceptual cost of overlapping keyed-storage contracts.

recommendation.title: Extend Existing Store Safely
recommendation.body: Add an explicit agent-scoped mode to `api.runtime.state.openKeyedStore` with declared capabilities, quotas, isolation, and lifecycle tests before allowing installed plugins to use it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged plugin-state SQLite migrations make this the strongest available routing signal for the storage ownership and migration side of the decision.
